steps.text: In a physical change, no new substance is formed — the material only changes its shape or state. Let's see one.
The ice melts into water, but it's still H₂O — same substance, just a different form. And you can freeze it back.
Folding paper, melting ice, dissolving sugar — all physical changes: same substance, different form, and usually reversible.

coach.mission: Try a change and check that no new substance is formed.
whenStuck: Tap an example like “Melt Ice”, then watch what happens.
Ask yourself: is it still the same substance afterwards?
whenWrong: In a physical change the substance stays the same — only its form changes.
Melted ice is still water (H₂O), so no new substance formed.
whenCorrect: Right — same substance, just a new form. That's a physical change.
Good — and it can usually be reversed.
coach.done: You've seen a physical change makes no new substance. Try another example, or move on when you're ready.
